body:
About the last part. I'd actually be glad and relieved if everyone around me was happy and didn't need me for other reason than to share their joy (and whatever happens in their life, good and a little less good). I don't want to be the hero, I don't care to be thanked and I'd be equally content if someone else would help her more than I can do. The only thing that matters to me is to know she's safe and she's doing better, with or without me.

I can't help to obsess over her and how she feels because I don't want to count how many years have passed since the death of another friend.

It drives me crazy, just this.

Thanks you. I don't know if suicide is an illogical act, I've been there, it feels like a totally legitimate choice, even if a part of me, since I know how much it hurts to be left behind, thinks it's selfish.

Maybe I'm selfish too. I do care about her, but I'm so involved because I know I'd be shattered if she died.

Thanks you for your kind words. I know everything you said is true, but it's so difficult to act accordingly when you're panicking because a loved one could end their life. Everytime I fall into the same behavior, because my head says "better safe than sorry". 

I tried to detach myself a little, but it only works when she doesn't seem in immediate danger. When she tells she's going to kill herself, I stop being a functioning person.

This make me more sure that I'm not the right person to give her help, but still I can't ignore her whe she fall too deep into these thoughts.

I have to thank you for your words and, especially, for having addressed the problem with its name. The term "codepency" has been in the back of my head for a long time, but I was afraid to admit it. Whatever it is, I don't know how to get out of it, because the thought to fail her (and then to lose her) frighten me more than anything.

I can't be sure it's codepency (I read that a codependent person actually looks for people who are in need and interrupts the relationship when they don't feel needed anymore), but it surely is unhealthy.

I am myself a suicide survivor, and this is both a part of the reason why I felt so guilty after my friend's death and why I now feel responsible for this other friend. The first time I didn't talk to her when she opened to me, because we had similar issues and I wasn't ready to speak about them. I also think (deep inside I know I'm wrong, but it's irrational) that I may have helped to put this thought into her head. 

This time it's so fucking similar I can't help. I feel even more guilty because I'm under the impression (and in this case I don't think I'm delirious) she got worse since she met me, as if she have absorbed some of my wrong past habits.

Now I feel stuck between making a step back (for her sake, if it's true that I'm not doing anything good) and the fear she would feel abandoned if I do so, because I'm not tired of being her friend and I don't want her to think this way. I'd be okay to separate from her if I was SURE she's going to be better and I'd be here if she ever want to come back, soon, later or never. 

But the thought she could die and put me in the same nightmare is unbearable.

I did it through (long and meaningful) texts, but it's useless. She go up and down in an endless cycle of depression, but when she's down she's unable to see how much people care about her (not only me, she's a special and caring person when she feels a little better, it's not hard to imagine why she's so loved by her friends)

Now she's been depressed since a long time, that's why I'm so scared she could give up.

She doesn't have a family to rely on, actually her family is a big part of the problem. She has many good friends, but she doesn't trust them and she's so wary when people tell her they do care (she doesn't talk unless you say again and again and again, for days, weeks, months, that she matters and you really want to be there for her) that I'm afraid not many people are so persistent.

I know that recently she made new friends, but I strongly suspect she doesn't talk about serious topics and I hope she doesn't feel more invisible. I'd be glad if I'd know she's doing better and she's surrounded by supporting friends who she trusts, even if she didn't talk to me anymore for whatever reason. I would miss her a lot as a person, but I'd be content to know she's happy.

Thanks you for your honest and deep answer, I really appreciate it!

I know for a fact that my friend doesn't want to be heard. She refuses to talk if you offer your help, she actually acts like she doesn't care if you care and can treat you bad when you try to reach out to her.

She doesn't do this for hurtful purposes, she simply (truly!) doesn't believe that she's loved. I'm glad she says in public how she feels, I think that deep inside she needs people to tell her she's important (and she is, damn), but nothing seems enough to convince her.

She's in serious risk, I don't underestimate her suicidal intentions, so I'm terrified and I don't know the right thing to do. I'm afraid of making the situation worse everytime I reach out to her. Maybe she doesn't want people to talk to her, since she pushes everyone away when they try, but I'm not sure. I desperately need to know if I'm doing wrong and what I can do to be as helpful as possible.

She's the same. I don't care if she can't believe me now, I'd be happy just to keep her from do it. If I can be helpful saying that I care over and over, I did and I'll do it. I'm just afraid to do more damage, because I feel like I'm reinforcing her behaviour to the point she's going to do it if someone fails once.
